2026-07-01: July 01, 2026, was a travel day. We travelled by plane from Washington Dulles Airport to London Heathrow to Amsterdam Schiphol airport. Then we caught a bus from the airport to Haarlem where we were to stay three days in the Brasss Hotel. It was an overnight flight, so we arrived on July 02. Before departing there was the inevitable busy rush to get the house and yard in order. And of course there was finishing laundry and calculating what we would need for the almost two months we would be away. All went relatively smoothly, and I had one large suitcase, Victoria had one carry-on suitcase, and we each had backpacks. We took an Uber to the airport driven by a very friendly driver. At the airport, we checked our bags, breezed through security, and found our way to the British Airways lounge.
2026-07-22:
July 22nd, 2026, was a travel day. We were to take the train from Flensburg Germany to the Copenhagen Denmark airport and then ride a regional train to Hässleholm Sweden where we would pick up our reserved rental car and drive to my house in Skanes Fagerhult. Simple… not.

Our travel day started okay with breakfast at the hotel and then a short cab ride to the train station. We arrived at our departure platform with time to spare and waited for the train. We people watched as a train on our same platform slowly filled with passengers and then right before the train departed there was an inevitable mad rush. We hoped our boarding would not be as chaotic as we watched that train pull out of the station. We were enjoying the calm feeling of being early and prepared.

Before the train was out of sight, there was a panicked yelp from Victoria as she suddenly realized that that was our train. Ugh. After a minute of berating herself, we proceeded to the ticket office to recover from our travel error. When asked, the friendly customer service staff greeted us with a smiling proclamation “the next train is in two hours”. Ugh, Ugh!

We went outside - strangely enough in good spirits - and found a bench in the park across the street to wait out our time. After an hour plus of being defecated on by a tree shedding flowers and seeing approaching rain or fog or something not sunny, we abandoned our bench and made our way back inside the train station to wait for our train to arrive. The train arrived and we recognized that it was our train and we boarded for the first leg of our journey to Sweden. What proceeded was a pleasant ride through the Danish countryside with an easy train change in Fredericia Denmark on the way to the train station at Copenhagen airport. At the airport we had to change platforms which took us through the airport. That brief two minutes in the airport immediately brought back so many memories of past travel to and from the US and the many family members that are no longer with me. I really do love being in that space.

We were able to catch an earlier train to Hässleholm and started contemplating how to get our rental car, but announced that our train was to terminate at Malmo central station and we would have to change trains to continue on to our final destination. After asking the conductor, we simply had to stay on the train until its terminus and walk across the platform to catch another train that would take us the rest of the way. Simple.

Using our keen powers of observation we managed to get off the train one stop early and walk across the platform to where we thought our next train would be. Do you remember that scene in the movie “Home Alone” where Catherine O'Hara realizes “We forgot Kevin”? That was us “We Got Off At The Wrong Stop!” We dashed back to the train as the conductor’s whistle signalled the trains imminent departure. I barely got back to our original train car and was met with a frowning conductor. Because Victoria had dashed back to a different train car, I was left alone to receive a lecture from the conductor about listening and the danger of closing train doors.

At the correct stop at Malmo Central we actually managed to get on the correct train at the correct time to the correct destination. Our train-ular adventure seemed to be winding down. As the train emptied, we were finally able to get a seat and start considering our next phase of travel from the train station to the rental car station. I had wisely chosen to pick up the rental car in Hässleholm station instead of the much more convenient Markaryd station because the rental office was open twenty-four hours a day. Hence my confusion when I received an email about the rental car pickup at a kiosk in the parking lot of a Volvo dealership. And where was this Volvo dealership in relation to the train station? Answer, not very close.

After some panic (me) and some calm, sturdy reassurance (Victoria) we found a route to the alleged dealership and started the 1 plus-mile walk with all of our luggage to the waiting rental car granting kiosk. Did I mention it was raining? Not too badly though. And actually, the walk was pleasant and the sidewalks and streets were empty.

We got to the kiosk without error or incident and used the magic of the kiosk to retrieve a key for a car that was nearby in a parking space. I had a “that was easy” moment and loaded the car. We were mobile!

Our first priority was groceries, actually coffee for the next morning, so I drove to the nearby ICA grocery store. On the way, I thoughtfully tested the brakes at a crosswalk where a pedestrian crossed seemingly out of nowhere. The brakes braked (very well) and the pedestrian lived on to stealthily cross crosswalks in the future.

At the grocery store we loaded up on what we thought we would need to start our four weeks in Sweden. Victoria was the hero using Google photo language translation to get the right items. At checkout, I was again amazed at the simplicity of Google wallet. How have I lived without it? Though its ease of use makes me wonder how long my money will survive with it.

After the store, we drove to the house through the beautiful pastoral Swedish countryside. It is very beautiful here and the fading light made it more so. Arriving at the house, we noticed the house was still standing, the yard was truly transitioning to meadow, and that I did remember to bring the key to open the front door. After hauling luggage and groceries into the house, we divided efforts. Victoria with dinner execution and me with two twin beds to queen bed execution.  With dinner and bed ready, we ate and then rested on our first Swedish day and it was good.
2026-07-23: July 23rd, 2026, was a day to adjust to our new home for the next four weeks in Skanes Fagerhult.
2026-08-05:
August 5th was a travel day to Jonkoping Sweden. We met with the owner of tour company Swike (Fredrik Ljunggren) to discuss options for a cycling tour for Sisterbike 2027.

Criteria for the trip:

We are looking for a tour the summer of 2027

We would prefer to schedule the tour after the high season – early to mid-august

The group size varies between 20 and 25 people.

The trip length is usually 8 to 10 days

Hotels

We prefer to stay in hotels multiple nights rather than have to relocate each day

We prefer upscale centrally located hotels that are a good value

Food

Alcohol not included except as listed below

Breakfasts included with hotel stays

Lunches included on cycling days (packed lunches or picnics)

Dinners at least half included

Nice welcome dinner with an alcohol toast

Premium farewell dinner with an alcohol toast

Cycling

Premium eBikes

Digital navigation (we use Ride with GPS)

Cycling distance per day should total 50 km plus or minus 10 km

At least six cycling days

Should include one or two non-cycling days

We prefer guided tours with vehicle support

General

We enjoy stops at historic or cultural points of interest

We would be interested in city walking tours and museums

—------------

Meeting

We had a good conversation and discussed a possible option with a ride along the Vattern and along the east part of the Gota canal. Generally his route looked good and would capture the heart of Sweden. There were many issues that needed resolution that he would have to look into. These include transport to and from Gothenburg (the proposed launch point), support costs, availability and capacity of hotels.

Concerns

He had not provided planning and support for a group close to our size

He was new to the business, so even though there have only been positive reviews, he only has a year of experience as a cycling tour operator

I was not sure of the attractiveness of the route or the safety

Follow-up Swike

He would provide a rough cost estimate and details of transfers and hotel cost

He provided loaner bicycles and a ride with gps map that we used to cycle part of the route (half of day one)

He provided a ride with gps map that we could drive more of the route (or near route) that would be part of the cycle tour

Follow-up Victoria and Hans

We cycled and we drove.

The proposed route is beautiful and has stops that are interesting

The proposed route was mostly set off from trafficked roads by separate bike paths or small rural roads with the exception of a small section that used to be the main route to Stockholm.

We did not like the eBike loaners. The saddle was uncomfortable after only a few hours and they seemed flimsy.

We visited towns and looked at hotels suggested and they looked good.

We ate at the proposed welcome dinner location and it was great.

Conclusion

Finally, as much as I liked the tour operator and what he provided, I think his newness to the industry and his lack of experience with large groups makes choosing Swike to provide for the group very risky. As a result, I would not recommend it for our group.
